title: Toucan Beaks Are Radiators: 1/20 of the Bird's Weight 🦜
description:
Why is a toucan's beak so huge? The toco toucan's bill is about a third of its length but mostly air inside, and a web of blood vessels lets it work like a radiator that dumps body heat when it's hot and holds it in when it's cold.

Sources:
https://www.nationalgeographic.com/science/article/toucan-play-at-reducing-the-heating-bill
https://www.smithsonianmag.com/science-nature/oversized-beak-keeps-toucan-cool-15023806/
https://jacobsschool.ucsd.edu/news/release/417

Animated in the Isometric Infographic style.

topic: Why is a toucan's beak so huge?
script:
A toucan's beak is secretly a radiator.
Here's why you never noticed.
That giant bill is a third of the bird's length,
but barely a twentieth of its weight.
It's mostly air.
Thin sheets of keratin, the stuff in your nails,
wrap a foam of tiny bone struts.
Now the clever part.
Under that shell runs a web of blood vessels.
When the toucan gets hot,
it pumps warm blood into the beak,
and the heat pours out into the air.
Scientists filmed it with a heat camera
and watched the beak light up.
When it's chilly, it shuts the flow off
and keeps that heat inside.
For short bursts,
almost all the heat it loses
goes out through that beak.
Be honest, would you trade your nose
for a radiator on your face?
key_facts: A toco toucan's beak is about one third of its body length (Wikipedia, Toco toucan beak)
The beak is only about 1/20 of the bird's mass; Wikipedia also cites under 3% (Wikipedia, Toco toucan beak)
Inside is a rigid foam of bony fibers and membranes under thin keratin tiles; 'the beak is mostly air' (UCSD, Meyers 2005)

Blood flow to the bill is adjusted to dump or keep heat; adults can cut bill heat loss to about 5% or briefly lose almost all body heat through it (Tattersall et al., Science 2009, via National Geographic)
Researchers used infrared (thermal) cameras to see the bill heat up (Tattersall et al. 2009)
